content: 1. Individuals living with HIV who are newly initiated on antiretroviral therapy (ART) should be evaluated for active tuberculosis (TB) disease using appropriate diagnostic tests. The term newly initiated refers to those who begin ART in accordance with national treatment guidelines during the reporting period. 2. Appropriate TB diagnostic testing refers to methods recommended by the World Health Organization (WHO). This ensures that individuals living with HIV who screen positive for TB symptoms are accurately diagnosed. 3. The percentage of people living with HIV who are newly initiated on ART and tested for TB, and subsequently diagnosed with active TB disease, is a critical indicator. This measures the proportion of individuals who undergo proper diagnostic testing and are confirmed to have active TB disease. 4. Once active TB disease is diagnosed, it is essential to promptly initiate TB treatment and provide high-quality clinical monitoring, as per national clinical guidelines, to ensure treatment completion. 5. Multi-month dispensing (MMD) of antiretroviral (ARV) medicines is a key component of care for people living with HIV who are established on ART. This approach improves health outcomes, supports long-term treatment adherence, and reduces unnecessary clinic visits, contributing to system efficiency. 6. The uptake of differentiated service delivery (DSD) ART models among people living with HIV who are newly eligible for such models is an important metric. It tracks the adoption of DSD ART models over time and helps identify trends in enrollment. 7. Retention in DSD ART models is monitored every 12 months after enrollment. This ensures that clinical outcomes are at least equivalent to those achieved with conventional care. 8. Viral load suppression among people living with HIV enrolled in DSD ART models is measured at six months, 12 months, and annually thereafter. This indicator enables monitoring of progress toward achieving the third 95 target in the UNAIDS 95-95-95 goals. 9. Data collection for these indicators relies on robust electronic health information systems or paper-based tools, depending on the facility's resources. Disaggregation by gender, age, key populations, and DSD model categories is essential for comprehensive analysis. 10. Reporting on these indicators supports efforts to expand access to multi-month dispensing, DSD ART models, and other person-centered HIV care strategies, ensuring that care meets the diverse needs of people living with HIV.
